page: Amazon Web Services c6id.metal is a bare-metal compute-optimized server engineered for high-concurrency and data-intensive tasks. Powered by 64 physical cores and 128 vCPUs across an Intel Xeon 8375C x86_64 processor clocked at 3.5 GHz, the bare-metal architecture grants direct hardware execution without hypervisor overhead. The configuration pairs these cores with 256 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a compute-aligned 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2 GB per core.

Hardware expansion includes 7600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage bundled directly onto the instance, alongside a high-throughput 50 Gbps baseline network link. The server integrates Intel acceleration features including AVX-512 with VNNI, VAES, and SHA-NI, though it lacks dedicated GPU hardware accelerators. Benchmark evaluations validate high multi-threaded throughput, reaching the top 10% in PassMark CPU score, extended instructions, and cryptographic operations, while Geekbench multi-core and Clang software compilation rank comfortably in the top 25%. In contrast, single-core metrics across stress-ng and Geekbench register in the middle 50% band.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of 128 dedicated execution threads paired with bundled multi-terabyte NVMe storage yields strong resource concentration for workloads requiring rapid local I/O alongside heavy computation. Tradeoffs center on average per-core speeds and the fixed 256 GB memory boundary, making it less viable for memory-footprint-heavy architectures. Primary workloads suited for c6id.metal include high-volume batch processing, CI/CD compilation, distributed database engines, image processing pipelines, and in-memory caches such as Redis.
description: Amazon Web Services c6id.metal is a bare-metal, compute-optimized instance delivering 128 dedicated vCPUs from a 64-core Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz on x86_64 architecture. The server incorporates 256 GB of DDR4 system memory, 7600 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD storage, and a 50 Gbps network interface, operating without an attached GPU accelerator. Benchmark evaluations place its multi-threaded processing, cryptographic functions, and AVX-driven instruction pipelines in the upper tiers, highlighted by strong scores in Clang compilation and PassMark testing, while single-core performance settles in the middle median. The combination of dense multi-core parallel compute, integrated high-capacity NVMe scratch space, and direct bare-metal access provides high operational efficiency for parallel compilation clusters, video encoding, Redis deployments, and transactional database workloads.
